name: IoT Atlas open reference dataset
description: Certification requirements, ecosystem compatibility, device models, troubleshooting guides, cloud platforms, brands and mobile apps for connected products.
citation: IoT Atlas. IoT Atlas open reference dataset. https://hi-spark.net/data/iot-atlas-open-dataset.json, retrieved 2026-10-14.

certifications.title: FCC equipment authorization
certifications.name: FCC equipment authorization
certifications.summary: U.S. equipment authorization rules for radio transmitters, intentional radiators and certain electronic products placed on the American market.
certifications.meaning: Any device that transmits radio energy in the United States normally needs an FCC authorization before it can be marketed or imported. Devices fall into Certification, Supplier’s Declaration of Conformity or verification routes depending on the radio technology.
appliesTo: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular and sub-GHz radios
Unintentional radiators such as switching electronics
Wireless modules and host devices that contain them
doesNotCover: Electrical safety, which is handled by NRTL listing such as UL or ETL
RF exposure to users unless the device is assessed against the exposure limits
Cybersecurity or privacy of the device or its cloud
checklist: Identify the correct authorization route for each radio
Test to the applicable FCC rule part at an accredited lab
Keep the FCC ID label and user manual statements accurate
Complete the supplier’s declaration or certification filing
List the module grant conditions when using a pre-certified module

certifications.title: ISED radio certification (Canada)
certifications.name: ISED radio certification (Canada)
certifications.issuer: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
certifications.summary: Canadian radio equipment certification and labelling rules, managed under the spectrum management programme of ISED.
certifications.meaning: Wireless products sold in Canada require an ISED certification number and the correct label wording, usually in both English and French. Test reports from an accredited lab are accepted through a recognised certification body.
doesNotCover: Canadian electrical safety approval (cUL or equivalent)
checklist: Select the correct RSS standard for the radio
Test and obtain a certification number from a recognised body
Apply the ISED label and bilingual user statements
Record the hardware and firmware version tested

certifications.title: CE marking under the Radio Equipment Directive
certifications.name: CE marking under the Radio Equipment Directive
certifications.issuer: Notified bodies and the manufacturer under EU law
certifications.summary: The Radio Equipment Directive 2014/53/EU is the main route to CE marking for wireless products sold in the European Union.
certifications.meaning: Manufacturers declare conformity, apply the CE mark and produce a technical file. From 1 August 2025 the delegated regulation on cybersecurity for internet-connected radio equipment adds mandatory security requirements.
appliesTo: Any product containing a radio transmitter
Devices that combine radio, GPS or cellular functions
Internet-connected radio equipment, including apps that control them
doesNotCover: A CE mark alone does not prove a product is secure or future-proof
Chemical or packaging obligations handled by RoHS, REACH and packaging rules
National spectrum restrictions that still apply inside the EU
checklist: Identify the applicable directives and harmonised standards
Decide whether a notified body is required
Build and retain the technical file for the required period
Sign the EU declaration of conformity
Apply the CE mark, importer details and language requirements

certifications.title: UKCA marking (Great Britain)
certifications.name: UKCA marking (Great Britain)
certifications.issuer: UK approved bodies and the manufacturer
certifications.summary: The UK conformity assessment marking used for most products placed on the market in Great Britain, with separate rules in Northern Ireland.
certifications.meaning: UKCA marking mirrors much of the EU framework after Brexit. The UK government has continued to recognise CE marking for most goods, but radio equipment, security products and labelling rules should be checked per product before shipping.
appliesTo: Radio equipment placed on the Great Britain market
Products where the manufacturer chooses the UKCA route
Importers and distributors holding stock in the UK
doesNotCover: Northern Ireland, where specific UKNI arrangements apply
EU market access, which still needs CE marking
Product-specific approvals such as gas or medical devices
checklist: Confirm whether CE or UKCA is the accepted route for your product
Use a UK approved body where third-party assessment is required
Keep the UK declaration of conformity with UK responsible person details
Apply the UKCA mark and correct labelling

certifications.title: Brazilian telecommunications homologation
certifications.name: Brazilian telecommunications homologation
certifications.summary: Homologation required before telecom and radio products may be sold or connected to Brazilian networks.
certifications.meaning: Anatel homologation is granted to a local representative, and the approved model is published with a homologation number that must appear on the product or in the manual.
appliesTo: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular and RF products
Devices that connect to public telecom networks
doesNotCover: INMETRO safety certification where the product also falls under that scope
Consumer warranty and after-sales law obligations
checklist: Appoint a Brazilian representative as a legal holder
Test at an accredited lab against the applicable Anatel acts
Register the product and obtain the homologation number
Display the number and keep the certificate current

certifications.title: Mexican telecommunications approval
certifications.name: Mexican telecommunications approval
certifications.summary: Mexican homologation for products that use the radio spectrum or connect to public telecom networks.
certifications.meaning: Approval is issued through a Mexican holder and results in a homologation certificate that must be referenced in labelling and documentation for the Mexican market.
appliesTo: Mobile phones, tablets, wearables and Wi-Fi devices
doesNotCover: NOM safety and efficiency rules that may also apply
Software services operated from outside Mexico
checklist: Confirm whether the product is homologable or exempt
Appoint the Mexican holder and file the application
Test against IFT technical provisions
Label the product with the homologation reference

certifications.title: KC certification (South Korea)
certifications.name: KC certification (South Korea)
certifications.issuer: National Radio Research Agency (RRA) under MSIT
certifications.summary: Korean certification for radio equipment, combining radio conformity and, in many cases, electrical safety and EMC approval.
certifications.meaning: KC certification uses different routes: conformity certification, registration or a supplier declaration, depending on the radio type and power. Certificates are held by a Korean representative.
doesNotCover: Korean e-waste and recycling registration, which is separate
checklist: Classify the equipment and choose the right KC route
Test to Korean technical standards
Appoint a Korean representative to hold the certificate
Apply the KC mark and Korean-language label statements

certifications.title: Japanese radio certification (Giteki)
certifications.name: Japanese radio certification (Giteki)
certifications.issuer: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC) through registered bodies
certifications.summary: Japanese technical conformity certification for radio equipment, commonly known as the Giteki mark and administered through registered certification bodies.
certifications.meaning: Radio equipment must be certified and carry the Giteki mark with the certification number. Products that include a certified module may still need their own certification if the module conditions are not met.
appliesTo: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, RFID and cellular devices
doesNotCover: Japanese electrical safety obligations such as PSE for certain power supplies
Telecom network connection approval beyond the radio function
checklist: Determine whether the module certification can be reused
Apply to a registered Japanese certification body
Label the Giteki mark and certification number
Keep the construction-protection documentation current

certifications.title: Taiwan NCC type approval
certifications.name: Taiwan NCC type approval
certifications.summary: Taiwanese type approval for low-power radio equipment and telecom terminal devices sold on the local market.
certifications.meaning: Approved products receive a NCC certification number and must carry the NCC mark. The application is normally filed by a Taiwanese representative company.
appliesTo: Mobile and wearable devices with radios
doesNotCover: Taiwan BSMI electrical safety and EMC certification, which is separate
checklist: Confirm whether approval is required for the radio band and power
Test at a recognised Taiwanese laboratory
File through a local agent
Apply the NCC mark and label content in Traditional Chinese

certifications.title: Australian and New Zealand RCM
certifications.name: Australian and New Zealand RCM
certifications.status: Mandatory for radio and mains products
certifications.summary: The Regulatory Compliance Mark shows that a product meets Australian and New Zealand radio communications and, where applicable, electrical safety requirements.
certifications.meaning: The supplier must be registered in the national database and hold test evidence for radio, EMC and safety requirements. Labelling rules differ between radio and electrical safety scopes.
doesNotCover: Telecommunications cabling or carrier connection approval
checklist: Identify whether radio, EESS or both schemes apply
Register as a responsible supplier
Hold compliant test reports with the required standards
Apply the RCM with the correct size and placement

certifications.title: Saudi SASO conformity
certifications.name: Saudi SASO conformity
certifications.issuer: Saudi Standards, Metrology and Quality Organization
certifications.summary: Product conformity used for goods entering Saudi Arabia, issued through the SABER platform with certificate of conformity procedures.
certifications.meaning: Importers must register the product and obtain the required certificates of conformity before customs clearance. Radio and telecom products also need CITC approval.
doesNotCover: CITC radio and telecom licensing, which is handled separately
checklist: Confirm the technical regulation that applies to the product
Register the product in SABER and select the conformity route
Test to the applicable Saudi standard or approved equivalent
Attach the certificate to each shipment

certifications.title: Eurasian EAC conformity
certifications.name: Eurasian EAC conformity
certifications.issuer: National accreditation bodies of the EAEU member states
certifications.summary: EAC conformity for products placed on the Eurasian Economic Union market, covering safety, EMC and, for some categories, radio requirements.
certifications.meaning: Products assessed against the relevant technical regulations, for example low-voltage, EMC and EMC-of-radio rules, receive an EAC declaration or certificate that is valid across the member states.
doesNotCover: Language requirements outside the technical regulations
checklist: Map the product against the applicable TR CU regulations
Decide between declaration and certification routes
Use an accredited body in a member state
Mark the product with the EAC mark and Cyrillic information where required

certifications.title: Indian BIS registration and WPC approval
certifications.name: Indian BIS registration and WPC approval
certifications.issuer: Bureau of Indian Standards and the Wireless Planning and Coordination wing
certifications.summary: Indian compliance typically combines BIS registration for electronics safety under the CRS scheme with WPC approval for wireless products.
certifications.meaning: BIS registration is issued to the manufacturer through the Compulsory Registration Scheme, while the WPC equipment type approval covers the radio interface. Both can be needed for one product.
appliesTo: Electronics covered by the CRS list
doesNotCover: Consumer packaging declarations outside the schemes
checklist: Check whether the product appears in the CRS schedule
Test in a BIS-recognised laboratory
Apply for WPC ETA for the radio module
Apply the standard mark once registration is granted

certifications.title: China SRRC and CCC approval
certifications.name: China SRRC and CCC approval
certifications.summary: Wireless products entering China normally require SRRC radio type approval, with CCC compulsory certification for categories on the CCC list.
certifications.meaning: SRRC approval covers the radio transmitter type, and CCC covers safety and EMC for products in scope. Both are held by a local entity and are checked at import and sale.
appliesTo: Products in the CCC catalogue, including some IT and AV equipment
doesNotCover: China RoHS packaging disclosure, which is a separate obligation
Cybersecurity review for critical network equipment
checklist: Determine SRRC scope and the radio test standard
Check whether the product is in the CCC catalogue
Appoint a local applicant and submit samples
Apply the SRRC code and CCC mark as required

certifications.title: North American safety listing
certifications.name: North American safety listing
certifications.issuer: UL, Intertek (ETL), CSA and other NRTLs
certifications.summary: Third-party product safety certification for the North American market, issued by a Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory.
certifications.meaning: Safety listing is not a single government mark: it is a certification issued by an NRTL against UL or CSA standards. Retailers, insurers and electrical inspectors commonly require it, and the mark must match the exact product and factory.
appliesTo: Mains-powered IoT devices, hubs and chargers
Components such as power supplies inside a device
doesNotCover: Radio approval, which is the FCC or ISED scope
Performance, privacy or cybersecurity of the product
Software updates that change the safety-relevant design
checklist: Identify the correct UL or CSA standard for the product
Submit samples and critical components to the NRTL
Accept the factory inspection programme for listed products
Report design changes that affect safety before shipping them

certifications.title: IEC and EN 62368-1 safety standard
certifications.name: IEC and EN 62368-1 safety standard
certifications.summary: The hazard-based safety standard that replaced IEC 60950 and IEC 60065 for audio, video, information and communication technology equipment.
certifications.meaning: Rather than prescribing construction, IEC 62368-1 requires the designer to identify energy sources and provide safeguards. It is the safety standard that most smart speakers, hubs, cameras and chargers are tested against.
appliesTo: Devices with mains or battery power and a charging interface
doesNotCover: Cybersecurity of the device or cloud
checklist: Classify energy sources and required safeguards
Check component ratings and creepage and clearance distances
Test abnormal and single-fault conditions
Review the standard edition used in each market certificate

certifications.title: EMC Directive 2014/30/EU
certifications.name: EMC Directive 2014/30/EU
certifications.issuer: Manufacturer under EU law, with notified bodies where required
certifications.summary: The European directive that requires equipment to limit electromagnetic emissions and to be immune to interference in its intended environment.
certifications.meaning: EMC is assessed separately from radio and safety. Products that contain radios are usually covered by the Radio Equipment Directive, which combines radio and EMC requirements in one file.
appliesTo: Electrical and electronic equipment with possible emissions
Devices with switching power supplies or motors
Equipment intended for residential, commercial or industrial environments
doesNotCover: Immunity performance guarantees in every real installation
checklist: Identify whether RED or EMC Directive applies
Test emissions and immunity against harmonised standards
Document the assessment and any applicable standards
Include EMC statements in the declaration and manual

certifications.title: IECEE CB Scheme certificate
certifications.name: IECEE CB Scheme certificate
certifications.summary: An international system that lets one safety test report and certificate be converted into national certifications in participating countries.
certifications.meaning: The CB Scheme reduces repeated safety testing across countries. A CB test certificate and report from one member body is accepted as the basis for national approval by other members, sometimes with national differences added.
appliesTo: Products needing safety approval in several countries
doesNotCover: Radio approvals, which are handled by national telecom schemes
Factory inspection regimes of individual schemes
checklist: Choose a CB test laboratory recognised in the target countries
Confirm national differences before testing
Request the CB certificate and full test report
Convert the report into national certificates where needed

certifications.title: IEC 60529 IP rating
certifications.name: IEC 60529 IP rating
certifications.summary: Ingress protection rating that describes resistance to dust and water, written as IP followed by two digits.
certifications.meaning: The first digit covers solids and dust, the second covers water. Ratings apply to the complete enclosure as tested, not to the electronics inside, and can be voided if the housing is opened or seals are reused.
appliesTo: Sensors exposed to humidity or rain
doesNotCover: Impact resistance, which is covered by IK ratings
Continued protection after repair or battery replacement
checklist: Select the rating required by the installation environment
Test the finished product, including seals and gaskets
Include cable glands and connectors in the assessment
State the test conditions in marketing material

certifications.title: CSA Group certification
certifications.name: CSA Group certification
certifications.summary: Canadian safety certification that is also accepted as an NRTL listing for the United States market.
certifications.meaning: CSA marks show that a product has been evaluated against Canadian and, where applicable, U.S. standards. This is often the most practical route for products sold in both countries at once.
appliesTo: Electrical and electronic products for Canada
Products seeking a combined Canada and U.S. listing
doesNotCover: Radio equipment certification in either country
checklist: Confirm which CSA or UL standards apply in each country
Choose a combined Canada and U.S. certification if possible
Keep the factory inspection programme current
Report changes to critical components

certifications.title: Restriction of Hazardous Substances
certifications.name: Restriction of Hazardous Substances
certifications.summary: Restricts lead, mercury, cadmium, hexavalent chromium and certain phthalates in electrical and electronic equipment sold in the EU.
certifications.meaning: RoHS compliance is shown through a technical file, supplier declarations and material test reports rather than a product mark. Many other markets have adopted similar restrictions, sometimes with different substance lists.
appliesTo: Electrical and electronic equipment in the ten RoHS categories
Components and sub-assemblies placed on the market
Cables, power supplies and accessories sold with the device
doesNotCover: Batteries, which have their own regulation
Packaging, which is covered by packaging rules
checklist: Collect supplier declarations and material test reports
Assess homogeneous material levels rather than the finished product
Keep evidence for every part number in the bill of materials
Refresh evidence when a supplier changes a material or process

certifications.title: REACH SVHC and SCIP notification
certifications.name: REACH SVHC and SCIP notification
certifications.summary: European chemicals regulation that places duties on suppliers when a product contains a Substance of Very High Concern above the threshold.
certifications.meaning: IoT hardware can contain SVHCs in solder, plastics, coatings or cables. Information duties apply at the article level, and SCIP database notification is required for articles placed on the EU market.
appliesTo: Finished articles placed on the EU market
doesNotCover: Restriction of hazardous substances in electronics, which is RoHS
checklist: Collect full material declarations from suppliers
Check the current SVHC candidate list regularly
Communicate information down the supply chain when required
Prepare SCIP notifications for the affected articles

certifications.title: Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment
certifications.name: Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment
certifications.summary: Rules that make producers responsible for financing the collection and recycling of electrical and electronic equipment.
certifications.meaning: Sellers that place products on the market usually have to register with a national producer responsibility organisation in each country, report volumes and display the crossed-out bin symbol.
appliesTo: Online sellers, including distance sellers into the EU
checklist: Register in every EU country where you place goods
Report put-on-market volumes on time
Print the crossed-out bin symbol and producer identification
Contract with a take-back scheme where required

certifications.title: EU Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542
certifications.name: EU Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542
certifications.summary: Replaces the older battery directive with wider duties covering carbon footprint, recycled content, labelling, due diligence and removability.
certifications.meaning: The regulation applies progressively, so different obligations start on different dates. Portable batteries designed into IoT products face removability and replaceability expectations, and labelling requirements expand over time.
appliesTo: Products with rechargeable or replaceable batteries
Producers placing batteries on the EU market
doesNotCover: Transport testing of lithium cells, which is UN 38.3
Safety testing of the battery pack
Recycling targets handled by national schemes
checklist: Identify the battery category and the applicable phase-in dates
Plan for removability and replaceability of portable batteries
Prepare carbon footprint and recycled content documentation
Apply the battery labelling and QR requirements when they apply

certifications.title: California Proposition 65
certifications.name: California Proposition 65
certifications.issuer: California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment
certifications.summary: California law that requires a clear warning when a product exposes users to chemicals on the state list above safe harbour levels.
certifications.meaning: The rule is warning-based rather than approval-based. Manufacturers either assess exposure and warn, or document that exposure is below the safe harbour level. Warning content and placement follow set formats.
appliesTo: Cables, vinyl materials, solder and coatings
Products where a chemical may be released during normal use
checklist: Screen the bill of materials against the current chemical list
Assess likely exposure routes and duration of use
Choose between a warning and a documented no-exposure case
Apply the warning in the required format and refresh the review

certifications.title: UN 38.3 lithium battery transport testing
certifications.name: UN 38.3 lithium battery transport testing
certifications.issuer: UN Manual of Tests and Criteria, tested by accredited labs
certifications.summary: Transport test requirement for lithium metal and lithium ion cells and batteries before air, sea or land shipment.
certifications.meaning: Shipping lithium batteries without a UN 38.3 test summary is a transport regulation violation, and carriers can refuse the shipment. The test report accompanies the battery through the supply chain, including sample shipments.
appliesTo: Devices with lithium ion or lithium metal cells
doesNotCover: Battery safety certification of the finished product
checklist: Test each cell and battery type as shipped
Hold the test summary from an accredited laboratory
Check state of charge and packaging rules for air transport
Re-test after design or supplier changes that affect the battery

certifications.title: Energy Star efficiency programme
certifications.name: Energy Star efficiency programme
certifications.summary: Voluntary efficiency labelling for products that meet Energy Star specifications in an eligible category.
certifications.meaning: For network equipment and consumer electronics, Energy Star certification requires third-party testing and registration, and the label must be used only for the certified configuration.
appliesTo: Eligible consumer electronics and network equipment
Products where efficiency is a selling point
Retail programmes that require the label
doesNotCover: EU energy labelling, which is a separate scheme
checklist: Confirm the product category is currently eligible
Test against the active specification version
Complete third-party certification and registration
Report changes that affect qualified configuration

certifications.title: ETSI EN 303 645 consumer IoT security baseline
certifications.name: ETSI EN 303 645 consumer IoT security baseline
certifications.issuer: ETSI, developed with industry and regulators
certifications.summary: Widely referenced baseline of thirteen security provisions for consumer IoT devices, from no universal default passwords to secure updates.
certifications.meaning: EN 303 645 is not a market access requirement by itself, but several national schemes and retailer requirements use it as the reference. Compliance is usually evidenced by a test report against the provisions plus the corresponding data protection guidance.
appliesTo: Consumer IoT devices such as cameras, hubs and sensors
Companion mobile apps and cloud services
Manufacturers designing a security baseline programme
doesNotCover: Industrial or medical device security requirements
Full ISO 27001 style management system certification
checklist: Eliminate universal default passwords and enforce unique credentials
Provide a vulnerability disclosure contact and process
Publish a support period and update policy
Secure sensitive data in transit and at rest
Test the device against the thirteen provisions

certifications.title: EN 18031 harmonised standards under the RED
certifications.name: EN 18031 harmonised standards under the RED
certifications.issuer: CEN/CENELEC standards, cited under the Radio Equipment Directive
certifications.summary: Harmonised standards that give a presumption of conformity with the cybersecurity requirements added to the Radio Equipment Directive.
certifications.meaning: With the delegated regulation applying from 1 August 2025, internet-connected radio equipment must meet network protection, personal data protection and fraud protection requirements. EN 18031-1, -2 and -3 are the main routes, and testing is done by notified bodies.
appliesTo: Internet-connected radio equipment in the EU
Wearables, cameras, toys and home devices with apps
Devices that process personal data or allow payments
doesNotCover: GDPR duties of the service operator
Security of back-end services outside the device scope
checklist: Confirm which of the three standards applies to the product
Map device features against each requirement clause
Engage a notified body early in the schedule
Keep the assessment in the technical file with the declaration of conformity

certifications.title: NIST IR 8259 IoT cybersecurity baseline
certifications.name: NIST IR 8259 IoT cybersecurity baseline
certifications.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
certifications.summary: A voluntary baseline of six foundational cybersecurity activities for connected devices, used widely in procurement and product planning.
certifications.meaning: NIST IR 8259 describes what a manufacturer should do before a device reaches the market, and 8259A lists the corresponding device capabilities. It is often used together with the IoT device cybersecurity guidance for federal acquisition.
appliesTo: Procurement requirements that reference NIST guidance
Products seeking a documented baseline for enterprise buyers
doesNotCover: Sector-specific regulation such as medical devices
checklist: Identify the device and its security assumptions
Define the customer-facing security capabilities
Document the update and vulnerability handling model
Map the device against the six activities and 8259A capabilities

certifications.title: US Cyber Trust Mark
certifications.name: US Cyber Trust Mark
certifications.summary: A voluntary US labelling programme for consumer IoT cybersecurity, developed from the FCC cyber labelling initiative.
certifications.meaning: The label is intended to give shoppers a simple signal that a device meets a defined security baseline, including unique passwords, updates and vulnerability handling. Programme details and the list of recognised administrators continue to develop, so the current requirements should be confirmed before planning a launch around the mark.
appliesTo: Consumer IoT products sold in the United States
Retailers and marketplaces that promote the label
Manufacturers planning a security differentiation strategy
doesNotCover: Radio equipment authorisation, which is separate
A substitute for privacy law compliance
checklist: Check the current programme scope and requirements
Align the device with the underlying security criteria
Plan for third-party testing and label administration
Keep a public support and update commitment

certifications.title: IEC 62443 industrial cybersecurity
certifications.name: IEC 62443 industrial cybersecurity
certifications.summary: A family of standards for cybersecurity of industrial automation and control systems, covering processes, systems and components.
certifications.meaning: IEC 62443 is the reference for industrial IoT, gateways and building systems. Buyers often require a security level target such as SL 1 or SL 2, and evidence is usually produced through a certification or an independent assessment.
doesNotCover: Consumer IoT baselines, which are lighter weight
checklist: Define the target security level and zones for the product
Apply secure development and hardening requirements
Document threat model, access control and update process
Complete an independent assessment or certification

certifications.title: Information security management (ISO/IEC 27001)
certifications.name: Information security management (ISO/IEC 27001)
certifications.summary: Certification of a management system for information security, covering how an organisation protects its own and its customers’ data.
certifications.meaning: ISO/IEC 27001 certifies the organisation and its processes, not a specific device. For IoT companies it is most relevant to the cloud service, the mobile app backend and internal development practices, and it is frequently demanded in B2B procurement.
appliesTo: Companies operating customer data at scale
Vendors responding to enterprise security questionnaires
doesNotCover: Privacy law compliance, which ISO 27701 addresses
checklist: Define the scope and statement of applicability
Assess risks and select controls
Operate the management system with evidence
Complete stage 1 and stage 2 audits and maintain surveillance audits

certifications.title: Privacy information management (ISO/IEC 27701)
certifications.name: Privacy information management (ISO/IEC 27701)
certifications.summary: An extension to ISO/IEC 27001 and 27002 for privacy information management, covering controllers and processors of personal data.
certifications.meaning: ISO/IEC 27701 provides a management framework that maps to privacy regulation, which is useful for IoT companies handling location, camera or health data. It complements but does not replace legal compliance.
appliesTo: Cloud services that process personal data
Mobile apps collecting usage or account data
Organisations acting as data processors for enterprise clients
doesNotCover: A guarantee of legal compliance in each jurisdiction
checklist: Start from an operational ISO/IEC 27001 management system
Identify the controller and processor roles
Extend the risk assessment to personal data
Document records of processing and retention

certifications.title: SOC 2 trust services report
certifications.name: SOC 2 trust services report
certifications.summary: An independent attestation report on controls covering security and, optionally, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality and privacy.
certifications.meaning: SOC 2 is a report rather than a certificate. Enterprise customers typically ask for a Type 1 point-in-time report first and a Type 2 report covering a period of operation as the service matures.
appliesTo: Cloud services and IoT platforms serving business customers
Mobile backend and data processing environments
checklist: Choose the relevant trust services criteria
Document policies and control evidence
Complete a readiness assessment before the audit
Publish the report under NDA to customers

certifications.title: EU General Data Protection Regulation
certifications.name: EU General Data Protection Regulation
certifications.summary: The core EU law on processing personal data, including data collected by connected devices, apps and cloud services.
certifications.meaning: IoT products routinely process personal data such as account details, device identifiers, location, camera footage or health measurements. GDPR requires a lawful basis, transparency, data minimisation, security, retention limits and support for data subject rights, and it applies to sellers outside the EU that target EU users.
appliesTo: Cameras, trackers and wearables that process personal data
Manufacturers and service providers offering devices to EU users
doesNotCover: Sector rules such as the ePrivacy Directive for cookies and communications
Local implementation laws that add national requirements
checklist: Map what personal data each product collects and where it goes
Define the lawful basis and document it
Publish a privacy notice that matches the actual data flows
Implement retention, deletion and export capabilities
Assess transfers outside the EU and the safeguards used

certifications.title: California consumer privacy rights
certifications.name: California consumer privacy rights
certifications.issuer: California Privacy Protection Agency and the Attorney General
certifications.summary: California privacy law giving consumers rights over personal information, including the right to know, delete, correct and opt out of sale or sharing.
certifications.meaning: Businesses meeting the thresholds must provide notices at collection, honour consumer requests and manage contracts with service providers. Device identifiers and precise location data count as personal information, so companion apps and cloud services are usually in scope.
doesNotCover: Sector rules such as health data laws
checklist: Confirm whether the business thresholds apply
Update the privacy notice and collection disclosures
Implement request handling and identity verification
Review contracts with analytics and advertising partners

certifications.title: Children’s online privacy (COPPA)
certifications.name: Children’s online privacy (COPPA)
certifications.summary: US rule that restricts collecting personal information from children under thirteen without verifiable parental consent.
certifications.meaning: Smart toys, kids’ watches and children’s cameras are a direct COPPA risk area because they combine cameras, microphones, location and app accounts. The rule also constrains third-party analytics and advertising in child-directed services.
appliesTo: Smart toys, kids’ watches and children’s trackers
Apps and services directed to children
Sites with actual knowledge of child users
doesNotCover: EU child data rules such as GDPR Article 8
checklist: Decide whether the product or app is child-directed
Minimise collection and disable behavioural advertising where required
Implement verifiable parental consent where needed
Provide parental review and deletion routes
Review vendor data flows for child data

certifications.title: Wi-Fi Alliance certification
certifications.name: Wi-Fi Alliance certification
certifications.summary: Certification programme that confirms a product interoperates with Wi-Fi networks and supports the security and feature set claimed on the package.
certifications.meaning: Certification covers the tested configuration, including the chipset, firmware and antenna design. Wi-Fi 6, Wi-Fi 6E, Wi-Fi 7, WPA3 and EasyMesh are separate programmes, and a device can carry more than one designation.
appliesTo: Access points, routers, extenders and mesh systems
Cameras, doorbells and appliances with Wi-Fi
Modules used as part of a certified end product
doesNotCover: Radio regulatory approval such as FCC or CE
Internet service quality or cloud performance
Mesh performance in every building layout
checklist: Choose the certifications that match the marketing claims
Test at an authorised laboratory using the correct test plan
Transfer the module certification conditions to the host design
Display the certification marks and identifiers correctly

certifications.title: Bluetooth qualification
certifications.name: Bluetooth qualification
certifications.summary: Membership, declaration and qualification process that lets a product use the Bluetooth trademarks and claim version support.
certifications.meaning: Products must be qualified through the Bluetooth SIG and listed, and the design must be declared by the member company. Component declarations from a module supplier can reduce the test scope but not the obligation to declare the final product.
appliesTo: Devices using Bluetooth Low Energy for setup or sensors
Modules embedded in a larger product
doesNotCover: Radio approval in the destination countries
checklist: Join the Bluetooth SIG as a member
Use qualified components and record their declarations
Complete the declaration and product listing
Keep the qualified design version aligned with shipped firmware

certifications.title: Matter certification
certifications.name: Matter certification
certifications.summary: Application-layer standard that lets smart home devices work across Apple Home, Google Home, Amazon Alexa and SmartThings.

doesNotCover: Cloud features of the vendor app

troubleshooting.title: Camera will not connect to Wi-Fi
troubleshooting.symptom: A security camera cannot join the local Wi-Fi network or repeatedly drops offline.
likelyCauses: 2.4 GHz-only camera paired to a 5 GHz network
Weak signal at the installation point
Wrong Wi-Fi password or security mode
Router isolation or guest network restrictions
Camera already paired to another account
quickChecks: Confirm the camera supports 2.4 GHz and/or 5 GHz
Move the camera near the router for setup
Confirm the password and SSID
Disable client isolation during setup
Remove the old device entry from the app if needed
steps: Factory reset the camera using the official procedure
Connect the phone to the intended 2.4 GHz network
Open the official app and start a fresh pairing
Enter the correct Wi-Fi credentials
Wait for the pairing confirmation before moving the camera
Test live view at the final installation point
troubleshooting.escalation: If the camera connects near the router but fails outside, improve Wi-Fi coverage with a mesh node or access point rather than repeatedly resetting the camera.

troubleshooting.title: Matter device will not pair
troubleshooting.symptom: The Matter setup code fails, the device is not discovered or pairing stops before completion.
likelyCauses: Device is not in pairing mode
Phone is on the wrong Wi-Fi or Thread network
Thread border router unavailable
Old controller firmware
Setup code already used or device still paired elsewhere
quickChecks: Confirm the device is Matter-certified
Check whether the device uses Wi-Fi or Thread
Update the controller and device firmware
Confirm Bluetooth is enabled during commissioning
Remove stale pairings from other ecosystems
steps: Reset the Matter device using the manufacturer procedure
Open the intended controller app
Scan the Matter QR code or enter the manual pairing code
Keep the phone near the device during commissioning
Complete naming and room assignment
Test local control before adding a second controller
troubleshooting.escalation: For Thread devices, verify that a compatible Thread border router is online and that IPv6 is enabled on the network.

troubleshooting.title: Zigbee device keeps going offline
troubleshooting.symptom: A Zigbee sensor, light or lock shows offline or responds slowly in the app.
likelyCauses: Weak mesh coverage
Hub or coordinator overloaded
Wi-Fi and Zigbee channel interference
Battery or power issue
Device dropped from the mesh
quickChecks: Check battery and power
Confirm the hub is online
Review Zigbee channel and Wi-Fi channel overlap
Check how many routers are in the Zigbee mesh
Test the device near the hub
steps: Bring the device near the hub and test
Re-pair it if it remains offline
Add a mains-powered Zigbee router device between hub and sensor
Move the hub away from the router and USB 3 devices
Rebuild or refresh the mesh if the platform supports it
troubleshooting.escalation: If only one room fails, treat it as a coverage problem first. If all devices fail, troubleshoot the hub, coordinator and channel plan.

troubleshooting.title: Smart Life cannot find a device
troubleshooting.symptom: A Tuya or Smart Life device is not discovered during pairing.
likelyCauses: Device is in a different pairing mode
Bluetooth or location permission is blocked
Device is paired to another account
App region or data center mismatch
Unsupported Wi-Fi band during commissioning
quickChecks: Confirm the correct app and account region
Enable Bluetooth and local network permissions
Place the device near the phone
Reset the device to pairing mode
Check whether it is already paired to another account
steps: Remove any previous device entry
Reset the device according to the manufacturer manual
Open the matching app and choose Add Device
Select auto-discovery or the correct category
Complete Wi-Fi credentials and wait for the device to register
Rename the device and test control
troubleshooting.escalation: If the device uses a manufacturer-specific white-label app, do not assume Tuya Smart or Smart Life will control it. Verify the app stated in the official manual.

troubleshooting.title: Ring doorbell shows offline
troubleshooting.symptom: The Ring doorbell appears offline or stops sending notifications.
likelyCauses: Weak Wi-Fi signal
Battery or power issue
Router or ISP outage
Ring service or account issue
Device needs restart
quickChecks: Check battery or wired power
Test Wi-Fi at the door location
Check the Ring status page and home internet
Confirm the device is not in setup mode
steps: Open the Ring app and check device health
Restart the router if other devices are offline
Power-cycle the doorbell using the official procedure
Reconnect to Wi-Fi if credentials or network changed
Test motion alerts and live view
troubleshooting.escalation: If only the doorbell is offline, focus on door-side Wi-Fi coverage, transformer power or battery condition.

troubleshooting.title: Camera does not detect the microSD card
troubleshooting.symptom: The camera app reports no storage, format failure or unusable local recording.
likelyCauses: Card format is unsupported
Counterfeit or worn card
Card exceeds supported capacity
Firmware bug
Card inserted incorrectly
quickChecks: Confirm the maximum supported capacity
Use a reputable card rated for continuous recording
Format the card in the camera or official app
Check the card on a computer
Update camera firmware
steps: Power off the camera
Remove and reinsert the card correctly
Let the camera or app format the card
Test recording locally
Replace the card if format or write operations still fail
troubleshooting.escalation: Continuous-recording cameras require high-endurance cards. A card that works in a phone may still fail in a camera.

troubleshooting.title: Smart lock calibration failed
troubleshooting.symptom: The lock app reports calibration failure, incorrect lock state or incomplete bolt travel.
likelyCauses: Door alignment or strike plate friction
Bolt not moving freely
Adapter or mounting issue
Battery level too low
Firmware or app calibration state
quickChecks: Check manual bolt movement
Inspect door alignment and strike plate
Replace batteries
Confirm the correct adapter and installation
Update firmware
steps: Calibrate with the door open
Check whether the bolt moves freely by hand
Adjust the strike plate or door alignment
Run calibration again
Test lock and unlock several times
Reinstall the app device entry only if calibration remains corrupted
troubleshooting.escalation: Do not force the motor. Friction in the door frame is a mechanical problem that software calibration cannot solve.

troubleshooting.title: IoT certificate rotation failed
troubleshooting.symptom: A device fleet cannot reconnect after a certificate expires or a rotation policy changes.
likelyCauses: Expired device certificate
Wrong CA chain
Clock skew on the device
Policy or thing registration mismatch
OTA rotation job failed
quickChecks: Check certificate validity dates
Confirm the device clock
Validate the CA chain
Compare device identity and policy in the cloud console
Test one pilot device before fleet rollout
steps: Identify the affected certificate and device group
Issue the replacement certificate
Test mutual TLS from one pilot device
Deploy rotation through a controlled OTA job
Monitor reconnect and error rates
Revoke the old certificate after the rollout
troubleshooting.escalation: Always keep a documented rollback path. Never rotate the entire fleet before validating DNS, time sync, TLS and the provisioning workflow.

troubleshooting.title: Robot vacuum cannot find its dock
troubleshooting.symptom: The robot cleans but cannot return to the charging dock, or it reports that it is lost.
troubleshooting.escalation: If the robot finds the dock from the app but not when it finishes a run, the saved map is usually stale: delete the map, relearn and re-add the no-go zones rather than moving the dock again.
appliesTo: Robot vacuums with a charging dock
likelyCauses: Dock moved after the map was saved
Dock power cable or adapter unplugged
Dock placed with obstructed approach or on a dark surface
Lidar or camera sensor covered with dust
Saved map out of date after furniture changed
quickChecks: Check that the dock light is on
Confirm the dock is on a hard, level surface with clear space in front
Wipe the sensors and charging contacts
Check the app for a lost or incomplete map
steps: Return the robot to the dock by hand and confirm it charges
Clean the dock contacts and the robot charging pads
In the app, delete and rebuild the map
Re-add no-go zones and room names
Run a short clean and watch the return-to-dock behaviour
Only then move the dock if placement is still wrong

troubleshooting.title: Smart plug shows online but does not switch
troubleshooting.symptom: The plug reports online in the app, but toggling it does nothing or the relay clicks and returns to the previous state.
troubleshooting.escalation: If the plug is warm, buzzes or trips a breaker, stop using it and replace it. Switching faults on mains hardware are a safety issue, not a software one.
likelyCauses: Firmware update in progress or failed
Local safety limit or power threshold triggered
Relay has reached end of life after heavy switching
Automation or schedule overriding manual control
Cloud or account state out of sync with the device
quickChecks: Try the physical button on the plug
Check the app for a firmware update prompt or error
Disable schedules and automations for that plug
Confirm the plug is not reporting over-temperature or over-power
steps: Press the physical button to test basic switching
Remove any schedule or scene for the plug
Update firmware and wait for the reboot
Power-cycle the plug at the socket for ten seconds
Re-test switching from the app
If the relay still does not hold, replace the plug

troubleshooting.title: Video doorbell sends no motion alerts
troubleshooting.symptom: Live view works but motion notifications never arrive on the phone.
troubleshooting.escalation: If alerts arrive while the app is open but never in the background, the phone is killing the app: check battery optimisation and background refresh for the app rather than reinstalling the doorbell.
likelyCauses: Notification permission disabled for the app
Sensitivity or motion zones set so the area is excluded
Phone battery optimisation stopping background alerts
Subscription feature expired or not enabled
Firmware bug after an update
quickChecks: Check the phone notification settings for the app
Open motion zones and sensitivity in the app
Confirm the doorbell is online in the app
Check whether alerts arrive with the app open
steps: Review motion zones, sensitivity and alert schedule
Enable background refresh and disable battery optimisation for the app
Update the doorbell and app firmware
Test in front of the doorbell with the app closed
If alerts never fire, reset the device and re-add it to the account

troubleshooting.title: The app cannot find a device because of the account region
troubleshooting.symptom: After moving, changing Wi-Fi or reinstalling the app, a device that used to work is invisible during pairing.
troubleshooting.escalation: Do not factory-reset the device before checking the region: a factory reset on a device bound to another region usually makes the problem worse and can delete local schedules.
appliesTo: Cloud accounts with regional data centres
likelyCauses: App account is registered in a different region than the device
Data centre selection changed during app installation
Device is still claimed by another account
Device was bought in a region whose server differs from the phone account
quickChecks: Check the account region in the app settings
Compare the app data centre with the country where you bought the device
Confirm the device appears offline rather than missing in the old account
Check whether the device is still bound to a previous owner
steps: Open the app settings and read the account region
If needed, register a second account in the device region
Remove the device from the old account first
Reset and pair the device on the matching region account
Document which account owns which device to avoid repeating this

troubleshooting.title: Streaming device or smart TV will not join Wi-Fi
troubleshooting.symptom: A TV, stick or streaming device cannot see the network or fails at the password step.
troubleshooting.escalation: If the TV connects to a phone hotspot but never to the home router, suspect the router security mode or band steering rather than the TV.
likelyCauses: Device supports only 2.4 GHz while the network name exists on 5 GHz
WPA3-only or mixed security mode not supported by older firmware
Special characters in the password rejected by the device keyboard
MAC filtering or access control list on the router
Router band steering hiding the 2.4 GHz SSID
quickChecks: Check the device specifications for the supported bands
Temporarily disable WPA3 or use WPA2/WPA3 mixed mode
Try the password on a phone keyboard to spot typing issues
Look for MAC filtering in the router settings
steps: Separate the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz SSIDs on the router
Connect the device to the 2.4 GHz network
If it fails, set the router to WPA2-PSK for the test
Temporarily disable band steering and access control
After the device connects, restore security settings one at a time

troubleshooting.title: Thread devices go offline when the border router is down
troubleshooting.symptom: Matter-over-Thread sensors and lights stop responding but their battery and app status look normal.
troubleshooting.escalation: Thread devices depend on a working border router and IPv6. If every Thread device fails at once, troubleshoot the border router and the network before touching individual devices.
appliesTo: Apple Home, Google Home and SmartThings Thread networks
likelyCauses: Border router unplugged or rebooting
IPv6 disabled on the router or ISP
Border router firmware out of date
Thread network credentials changed after a hub reset
Device dropped from the Thread network
quickChecks: Check that the border router is powered and online
Confirm the hub shows in the app as a Thread border router
Check whether other Thread devices respond
Look for a recent router or ISP change affecting IPv6
steps: Power-cycle the border router and wait for it to rejoin
Confirm Thread is enabled in the hub settings
Re-test one device near the border router
If only one device fails, remove and re-add that device
If all devices fail, reset the Thread network and re-add devices in order

troubleshooting.title: Bluetooth device will not pair with the phone
troubleshooting.symptom: A wearable, lock or sensor in pairing mode never appears in the app or in the phone Bluetooth list.
troubleshooting.escalation: If the device pairs with another phone, the problem is the phone or the app permission, not the device firmware.
appliesTo: Sensors that pair over Bluetooth Low Energy
likelyCauses: Bluetooth or location permission denied for the app
Device still bonded to another phone
Device not actually in pairing mode
Phone Bluetooth stack needs a restart
Interference or too much distance during pairing
quickChecks: Turn Bluetooth off and on again
Check app permissions for Bluetooth and location
Confirm the device LED pattern for pairing mode
Try pairing from the phone settings instead of the app
steps: Remove the old bond for the device in phone settings
Force-close the app and reopen it
Put the device back into pairing mode and pair within one metre
Complete the pairing inside the vendor app so the account is linked
If it still fails, test with a second phone to isolate the cause

troubleshooting.title: Firmware update stalls at a percentage
troubleshooting.symptom: An over-the-air update sits at the same percentage for a long time, fails, or the device becomes unresponsive afterwards.
troubleshooting.escalation: Never power off a device mid-update on purpose. If it is unresponsive after twenty minutes, follow the vendor recovery procedure rather than repeatedly cutting power.
appliesTo: Devices updated over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth
likelyCauses: Unstable Wi-Fi or low signal during download
Battery below the required level for the update
Interrupted by a reboot, power cut or app being closed
Update server or CDN issue
Device storage or partition too full for the image
quickChecks: Confirm the device is on stable power or above 50 percent battery
Check Wi-Fi signal strength at the device
Look for a second staged update that must run after the first
Check the vendor status page for an outage
steps: Move the device closer to the router for the update
Keep the app in the foreground and the phone unlocked
Let the update finish; a stalled progress bar can still complete
If it fails, retry once from the app and not by power cycling
On repeated failure, use the vendor recovery or USB update path

troubleshooting.title: Voice assistant says the device is not responding
troubleshooting.symptom: Alexa or Google Assistant reports that the device is not responding even though the vendor app controls it fine.
troubleshooting.escalation: If a renamed device breaks voice control but the app works, the fix is discovery and naming, not re-pairing the device.
appliesTo: Devices renamed or moved to another room
likelyCauses: Device renamed in the vendor app after discovery
Account link expired or password changed
Skill or integration removed and re-added
Duplicate device names in the same home
Region or language mismatch in the assistant account
quickChecks: Test the device in the vendor app first
Say the exact device name as it appears in the assistant app
Check the linked account status in the assistant app
Look for duplicate entries with the same name
steps: Confirm the device works in the vendor app
Re-run device discovery in the assistant app
Rename devices so each name is unique in the home
Re-link the account if the status shows an error
Disable and re-enable the skill or integration if discovery fails

troubleshooting.title: Camera night vision is washed out or stays in black and white
troubleshooting.symptom: At night the image looks washed out, shows a bright ring, or the camera never switches to infrared.
troubleshooting.escalation: A washed-out night image through glass is a reflection problem: move the camera behind the glass or switch off the IR LEDs instead of replacing the camera.
likelyCauses: Camera mounted behind a window causing IR reflection
IR LEDs disabled in the app or on a schedule
Dust, cobwebs or water on the lens or IR ring
Nearby light source defeating the day/night threshold
Hardware fault in the IR cut filter after long use
quickChecks: Check the night vision setting in the app
Clean the lens and the ring of IR LEDs
Look for a bright spot or halo in the image
Test with the room in complete darkness
steps: Clean the lens and IR ring with a dry microfibre cloth
Set night vision to auto in the app
Remove the camera from behind glass if a halo appears
Adjust nearby lights so the camera is not fooled into day mode
If the image stays colour in darkness, the IR cut filter is likely faulty

troubleshooting.title: Smart lock battery drains in days
troubleshooting.symptom: A battery-powered smart lock reports low battery far sooner than the expected months of use.
troubleshooting.escalation: If the lock is warm around the battery compartment or the drain continues with a fresh set of the recommended cells, stop using it and contact the manufacturer: internal drain on mains-free hardware is a safety matter.
likelyCauses: Motor straining against a misaligned strike plate
Wrong battery chemistry or brand (alkaline vs lithium requirements)
Wi-Fi or Matter polling more often than the lock supports
Frequent auto-unlock or geofence triggers
Firmware bug or repeated pairing attempts
quickChecks: Check whether the bolt moves freely by hand
Confirm the battery type in the official manual
Review auto-unlock and geofence settings
Look for repeated reconnect or pairing events in the app
steps: Lubricate and align the bolt, strike plate and frame
Fit the exact battery type the manual requires
Disable auto-unlock and geofence rules temporarily
Re-seat the lock in the app or reset it once
Monitor drain for one week with the new settings
If drain continues, escalate to the manufacturer

troubleshooting.title: Camera live view lags or keeps buffering
troubleshooting.symptom: Live view opens but stutters, drops frames or takes many seconds to start.
troubleshooting.escalation: If the camera lags at high resolution but is smooth in the low-bandwidth stream, this is throughput rather than a camera fault: fix Wi-Fi coverage or use the substream.
likelyCauses: Weak Wi-Fi signal at the camera
Upload bandwidth saturated by other devices
Streaming the main high-bitrate stream instead of the substream
Camera overheating in direct sun
Cloud relay or account region adding latency
quickChecks: Check reported Wi-Fi signal strength in the app
Try the lower-resolution stream
Test live view with other devices idle
Compare app performance on mobile data
steps: Move the camera or add an access point closer to it
Set live view to the substream for everyday checking
Cap the camera bitrate or resolution in the app
Update firmware and reboot the router and camera
If lag persists, test with a local NVR or SD recording to isolate the network

troubleshooting.title: Zigbee device will not pair with the hub
troubleshooting.symptom: A Zigbee sensor or light never joins the hub, or it joins and immediately drops.
troubleshooting.escalation: If a device pairs near the hub but drops in place, it is a mesh coverage problem: add a mains-powered Zigbee router instead of repeatedly resetting the device.
likelyCauses: Device not held in pairing mode long enough
Wrong hub mode or channel after a hub firmware update
Distance or wall construction blocking the join
Device already paired to another hub
Battery too low for the join process
quickChecks: Confirm the pairing LED pattern from the manual
Bring the device next to the hub and retry
Check hub firmware version
Replace the battery before pairing
steps: Remove the device from any previous hub
Reset the device to factory state
Put the hub in add-device mode and pair within one metre
Move the device gradually to its final position
If it drops at distance, add a mains-powered Zigbee router between hub and device

troubleshooting.title: Hub forgets devices after a power cut
troubleshooting.symptom: After an outage the hub comes back but several devices show offline or missing.
troubleshooting.escalation: If devices disappear after every outage, protect the hub with a small UPS or check the hub power supply rather than re-adding devices each time.
likelyCauses: Hub rebooted faster than the devices re-joined the mesh
Devices with weak batteries failed to rejoin
Network name or IP change after the outage
Corrupted local database after an unclean shutdown
Router took longer than the hub to come online
quickChecks: Wait ten minutes and refresh the app before reacting
Check whether the hub is online in the app
Confirm the router and internet came back first
Look for devices that also lost battery level readings
steps: Reboot the router first, then the hub
Wait for the mesh to re-form and refresh the app
Re-add only the devices that stay offline
Update hub firmware
Add a small UPS for the hub and router to avoid unclean shutdowns

troubleshooting.title: Camera motion alerts fire constantly
troubleshooting.symptom: Motion notifications trigger on swaying trees, headlights or rain instead of real events.
troubleshooting.escalation: If alerts only stop when detection is disabled entirely, the camera is mounted facing a trigger you cannot mask: move the camera or narrow the detection area rather than turning detection off.
likelyCauses: Detection zones covering roads, trees or reflections
Sensitivity left at maximum
PIR sensor aimed at a heat source or moving shadow
Notification schedule disabled so alerts fire all day
Person detection not enabled where available
quickChecks: Review the detection zone drawing in the app
Check sensitivity level
Look at the alert thumbnails to spot the trigger
Confirm whether person or vehicle detection is available
steps: Redraw the detection zone to exclude the trigger
Lower sensitivity one step at a time
Enable person or vehicle filtering if the model supports it
Set an alert schedule for the hours you care about
Test for two days before adjusting again

troubleshooting.title: Smart bulb flickers or buzzes
troubleshooting.symptom: An LED smart bulb flickers, buzzes or glows faintly when switched off.
troubleshooting.escalation: If the bulb flickers only on one fixture, the fixture or dimmer is incompatible. Check the bulb specification before replacing the bulb.
likelyCauses: Non-dimmable bulb on a dimmer
Dimming below the bulb minimum load
Neutral wire missing on a smart switch
Firmware dimming curve not suited to the fixture
Old wiring or a failing driver in the fixture
quickChecks: Confirm the bulb is dimmable and the dimmer type it supports
Test the bulb in a plain on/off socket
Check the minimum load for the switch
Look for a firmware dimming setting in the app
steps: Test the bulb in a non-dimmable socket
If it is fine there, check dimmer compatibility
Set a minimum brightness floor in the app
Update bulb and switch firmware
If flicker persists on one fixture only, replace the dimmer with a compatible model

troubleshooting.title: Wired doorbell does not ring the existing chime
troubleshooting.symptom: The doorbell works in the app but the indoor mechanical chime no longer rings.
troubleshooting.escalation: Never bridge or bypass a transformer above its rating to force a chime to work. If the chime needs more power than the transformer supplies, upgrade the transformer instead of rewiring around it.
likelyCauses: Transformer voltage below the doorbell requirement
Indoor chime not enabled in the app settings
Chime kit not installed or miswired
Digital chime not supported by the doorbell model
Existing chime mechanism worn out
quickChecks: Check transformer voltage and rating
Look for an indoor chime toggle in the app
Confirm the chime kit wiring from the manual
Test the chime by shorting the terminals briefly with care
steps: Read the doorbell power requirements from the official manual
Check the transformer rating printed on the unit
Enable the indoor chime in the app and set the duration
Reinstall the chime kit following the manufacturer diagram
If it still fails, have an electrician upgrade the transformer

troubleshooting.title: Camera microSD card fills up in days
troubleshooting.symptom: Local storage wraps or stops recording much sooner than expected.
troubleshooting.escalation: If a high-endurance card still fills in days, the recording profile is the cause: switch to event-only recording instead of buying a larger card.
likelyCauses: Continuous recording enabled instead of events
High bitrate or high resolution profile
Too many false motion events triggering clips
Card capacity small for the recording profile
Card wearing out and remounting repeatedly
quickChecks: Check whether recording mode is continuous or event-based
Review resolution and bitrate settings
