troubleshooting.title: Smart plug turns off on its own
troubleshooting.symptom: A plug or switch cuts power at random times without a scheduled action.
troubleshooting.escalation: If the plug switches off under load and is warm, treat it as an overload or hardware fault and stop using it until an electrician checks the circuit.
likelyCauses: Overload protection tripping under heavy load
Automation, timer or power threshold rule still active
Firmware restart after a failed update
Loose wiring in the plug or socket
Cloud outage leaving the device in a safe state
quickChecks: Note the load connected when it switches off
Check the plug temperature
Review all scenes, timers and power rules
Check firmware version and recent restarts
steps: Disconnect the load and test switching with no load
Delete every automation and timer for that plug
Update firmware and reboot the plug
Move the load to another circuit to compare
If it still trips, replace the plug or have the circuit checked

troubleshooting.title: Fitness band or watch does not sync steps
troubleshooting.symptom: The band shows steps on the screen but the app keeps yesterday's numbers or stays empty.
troubleshooting.escalation: If only one metric fails to sync, the problem is usually app permissions or the phone killing the app in the background, not the sensor itself.
likelyCauses: Health platform permission denied for the app
Background sync blocked by battery optimisation
Bluetooth disconnected after the app was closed
Multiple apps claiming the same health data
Wearable storage full of unsynced records
quickChecks: Open the app and force a manual sync
Check health permissions for the app
Confirm Bluetooth is on and the band is connected
Look for a firmware update for the band
steps: Force a manual sync and note whether it completes
Grant health and background permissions to the app
Exclude the app from battery optimisation
Reboot the band and the phone
Disconnect other apps from the same health platform and retest

troubleshooting.title: Alexa skill will not link the vendor account
troubleshooting.symptom: During skill linking the login page loops, rejects the password or reports that the account cannot be linked.
troubleshooting.escalation: If linking fails on the vendor site as well as in Alexa, the account itself is the problem: reset the vendor password first rather than unlinking the skill repeatedly.
appliesTo: Alexa skills for cameras, lights and plugs
likelyCauses: Wrong account type: social login versus email account
Password changed on the vendor side
Region mismatch between vendor and assistant accounts
Vendor service outage
Too many failed attempts triggering a temporary lock
quickChecks: Log in to the vendor app with the same credentials
Check whether the account uses single sign-on
Confirm the vendor region setting
Check the vendor status page
steps: Reset the vendor password and log in to the vendor app
Remove the skill or integration from the assistant
Re-add the skill and link again
Use the provider login if single sign-on applies
Wait out a temporary lock, then retry

troubleshooting.title: Camera two-way audio does not work
troubleshooting.symptom: You hear the camera but the person at the camera cannot hear you, or the audio is distorted.
troubleshooting.escalation: If audio works on a phone call but not in the camera app, the microphone permission belongs to the app, not the camera.
likelyCauses: Microphone permission denied for the app
The talk control must be held while speaking on some models
Audio muted in the app or by privacy mode
Phone busy in a call or using the microphone elsewhere
Camera speaker volume set very low
quickChecks: Check microphone permission for the app
Confirm you are holding the talk control
Look for a privacy or mute mode switch
Close other apps using the microphone
steps: Grant microphone permission to the camera app
Hold the talk button and speak after the prompt tone
Increase speaker volume in the camera settings
Disable privacy mode if enabled
Test from a second phone to isolate the handset

troubleshooting.title: Robot vacuum leaves streaks or puddles
troubleshooting.symptom: After mopping the floor shows streaks, wet spots, or the robot stops moving on wet flooring.
troubleshooting.escalation: If the robot leaks while docked, stop using the water tank and check the tank seal: internal leaks can damage the electronics.
appliesTo: Robots with a water tank or dock
likelyCauses: Dirty or worn mop pad
Water flow set too high
Pad not installed flat or already saturated
Floors not vacuumed before mopping
Wheel slip on wet flooring
quickChecks: Check the mop pad condition and fit
Review the water flow setting
Vacuum before mopping
Look for leaks around the tank
steps: Wash or replace the mop pad
Lower the water flow
Run a vacuum-only pass first on dirty floors
Re-seat the tank and check the seal
Run a test cycle in one room and inspect the result

troubleshooting.title: Smart lock keypad stops accepting the code
troubleshooting.symptom: The keypad lights up but the stored code no longer unlocks the door, or codes are only rejected at certain times.
troubleshooting.escalation: If the keypad fails while the battery is low, replace the batteries before changing codes: low power causes partial reads rather than clean failures.
likelyCauses: Battery below the level the keypad needs
Code removed or overwritten in the app
Keypad membrane wet or contaminated
Firmware update interrupted
Auto-lock or privacy mode blocking entry
quickChecks: Check the battery level in the app
Test app remote unlock, which uses the radio instead of the keypad
Dry the keypad and retry
Confirm the code still exists in the app
steps: Replace the batteries with the recommended type
Re-add the entry code in the app
Wipe the keypad dry and retest
Update firmware with the door open
Test keypad and app unlock before relying on it again

troubleshooting.title: Wearable heart rate readings look wrong
troubleshooting.symptom: Heart rate during exercise is far lower or higher than expected, or the sensor reports large jumps.
troubleshooting.escalation: Consumer wearable heart rate is not a medical measure. If the readings matter clinically, use a validated monitor and consult a professional.
likelyCauses: Strap or ring too loose so the sensor loses contact
Sensor covered by dirt, sweat or a tattoo
Worn over the wrist joint instead of above it
Firmware changing the measurement algorithm
Movement artefact during weights or rowing
quickChecks: Check fit and position
Clean the sensor area
Compare at rest against a manual pulse
Check for a firmware update
steps: Tighten and reposition the device above the wrist bone
Clean the sensor and the skin
Update firmware
Test during steady cardio rather than intervals or weights
If readings stay erratic, arrange a service check

troubleshooting.title: Smart plug reports no energy data
troubleshooting.symptom: The plug switches fine but the power or consumption figures stay at zero or are missing.
troubleshooting.escalation: If readings show a fixed value that never changes, the metering chip may have failed: no app calibration will fix that.
likelyCauses: Load too small for the metering range
Firmware without metering for that model
App unit or tariff settings not configured
Local safety limit shown instead of a measurement
Hardware metering fault
quickChecks: Connect a larger known load and watch the reading
Check the model specification for metering
Review units and tariff settings
Update firmware
steps: Test with a load the meter is designed for
Confirm the model actually meters power
Configure units and tariff in the app
Update firmware and re-check
If the reading never changes, request a warranty replacement

troubleshooting.title: Battery video doorbell drains in days
troubleshooting.symptom: A battery doorbell needs charging far more often than the expected months of use.
troubleshooting.escalation: If the doorbell still drains after disabling detection and lowering stream quality, the radio path or the battery is the cause: check signal strength and battery health.
likelyCauses: Too many motion events on a busy street
Weak Wi-Fi forcing higher transmit power
Live view used frequently
Cold weather reducing battery capacity
Old or non-recommended battery chemistry
quickChecks: Check the event count per day
Review signal strength in the app
Note the outside temperature
Check battery health or cycle count if reported
steps: Reduce detection zones and sensitivity
Lower live view resolution and clip length
Move the router or add an access point closer to the door
Update firmware
Replace aged batteries with the recommended type and re-measure daily drain

troubleshooting.title: Camera image is blurry or out of focus
troubleshooting.symptom: Footage looks soft even in daylight, or only part of the frame is sharp.
troubleshooting.escalation: If only one area of the frame is sharp, the lens is fixed-focus: reposition the camera or choose a model suited to the distance.
likelyCauses: Dome or glass cover scratched or dirty
Protective film left on the lens
Condensation behind the lens cover
Subject closer than the minimum focus distance
Dirty housing reducing contrast
quickChecks: Clean the lens cover with a microfibre cloth
Check for a protective film
Look for condensation inside the housing
Test focus at different distances
steps: Clean the lens and housing
Remove any transit film
Let the camera dry if condensation is present and check the seal
Reposition the camera to suit the subject distance
Compare with a second camera before replacing

troubleshooting.title: Matter commissioning code is rejected
troubleshooting.symptom: The controller says the pairing code is wrong, expired or already in use.
troubleshooting.escalation: If the code was already used, the device is still claimed by the previous controller: remove it there first rather than retrying the code.
likelyCauses: Code already used to commission the device elsewhere
Typing errors in the manual pairing code
Device not reset to commissioning mode
Controller firmware too old for the device
Thread border router unavailable for Thread devices
quickChecks: Check whether the device already appears in another ecosystem
Verify the digits on the label or in the app
Confirm the LED shows commissioning mode
Update the controller app and hub firmware
steps: Remove the device from any ecosystem that already has it
Reset the device to commissioning mode
Choose add device in the controller app
Enter or scan the code once, without blind retries
For Thread devices, confirm the border router is online first

troubleshooting.title: Wi-Fi slows down with many smart devices
troubleshooting.symptom: Smart plugs and cameras drop offline as more devices are added, and phones slow down in the same rooms.
troubleshooting.escalation: If the router has reached its client limit, device tweaking will not help: add an access point or a dedicated IoT network instead of resetting devices.
appliesTo: Homes with 40 or more connected devices
likelyCauses: Client limit reached on the router or band
2.4 GHz band congested with small devices
Single access point covering too large an area
DHCP pool too small for the number of devices
Cheap devices holding connections open
quickChecks: Count connected devices in the router interface
Check which band each device uses
Look for DHCP address exhaustion messages
Test whether drops correlate with adding devices
steps: Raise the DHCP pool or shorten lease times
Move IoT devices to the 2.4 GHz band or a guest network
Add an access point or mesh node
Update router and device firmware
Replace devices that repeatedly rejoin the network

troubleshooting.title: Solar panel does not keep the camera charged
troubleshooting.symptom: A solar-powered camera keeps losing charge even on sunny days.
troubleshooting.escalation: If a multimeter shows panel output but the camera never charges, the charging circuit or cable is faulty rather than the panel.
likelyCauses: Panel in shade or at the wrong angle for the season
Dirty or snow-covered panel
Cable or connector corroded or loose
Low winter sun plus heavy event traffic
Panel undersized for the camera power draw
quickChecks: Check panel orientation and shading through the day
Clean the panel
Inspect the cable and connector
Review daily power consumption
steps: Reposition and tilt the panel towards the midday sun
Clean the panel and check cable and connector
Reduce event traffic and live view use
Update firmware and read the charge log
Measure panel output if the battery still drops, then replace the faulty part

troubleshooting.title: GPS tracker reports the wrong location
troubleshooting.symptom: A tracker shows a location hundreds of metres off, jumps between places or stops updating.
troubleshooting.escalation: If the tracker is accurate outdoors but drifts indoors, the position comes from Wi-Fi or cell positioning rather than GPS: judge accuracy by the reported method.
likelyCauses: Indoor use where GPS is blocked
Assisted positioning using Wi-Fi or cell towers
Low battery forcing less frequent fixes
Poor sky view in cities or under cover
Firmware or platform mapping delay
quickChecks: Compare the reported accuracy value in the app
Check whether the device reports LTE, Wi-Fi or GPS fixes
Test outdoors with a clear sky view
Note the update interval setting
steps: Force a manual location update outdoors
Check the reported positioning method and accuracy
Adjust the update interval and battery mode
Update firmware
If the device never gets a GPS fix outdoors, request a service check
